summary: Teams create a digital game that teaches players about personal finance and money management, including budgeting, saving, investing, and making financial decisions. The game must be educational, engaging, and based on real-world scenarios, and teams present their game to judges. Teams must submit a combined PDF with required documentation and a clickable URL to the game before the deadline.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing all required items
No changes can be made to the project after the date of submission
Team ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Team ID cannot be accepted
presubmit_items: Clickable URL to Game (may include Artwork, Executable File, Storyboard, etc.)
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation
competencies: Design engaging and balanced gameplay mechanics using player-experience, data-driven methods, and continuous refinement
Develop clear rules and embed essential information within gameplay through integrated tutorials and visual cues
Integrate storyline and scoring systems to enhance player engagement and progression
Deliver game prototype and presentation to highlight key features and explain design

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.
Team submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing URL to Project Files, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual and BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage & Documentation Form.

rubric.description: Rules are consistently applied and well-integrated.
Educational content is engaging and insightful.
Conditions are clear and enhance gameplay.
Design is polished, thematic, and engaging.

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, use appropriate gestures and body language, and vary their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, and each team contestant's role is clear and integrated into the presentation. Transitions between speakers and/or points are smooth.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team and must take place within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at the NLC; however, contestants/teams may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
Finals may be part of the competition
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any middle level contestant may enter this judged team event
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic, the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines or Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified
